source: Live SPM Jira descriptions read on 1 October 2026. AC numbers are their displayed bullet order; Jira bullets are not separately numbered.

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Repository created, with all team members and both instructors granted access
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Branch naming and commit conventions documented in the repository
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: A pull request is required before merging to main, with at least one reviewer
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Definition of done agreed and recorded where the whole team can see it

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: A developer can clone the repository and start both applications by following the README
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: The backend exposes a health check that returns success
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: The frontend can call the backend successfully in local development

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Pipeline triggers automatically on every pull request
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Pipeline builds the application and runs the automated test suite
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: A failing test blocks the merge
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: The pipeline result is visible on the pull request

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Can log in with valid credentials and arrive at the landing page for my role
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Invalid credentials are refused, with a message that does not reveal whether the email address exists
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Can log out, after which protected pages are no longer reachable without logging in again

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Every account holds exactly one of: Event Organiser, Event Coordinator, Venue Staff, Technical Support Staff, Attendee
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Only Technical Support Staff can set or change the role on an account
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: The role is visible on the user's profile

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: An action attempted outside the user's role is refused
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Refusal does not depend on the user simply not seeing the button
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Requests from users who are not logged in are refused

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: My events list shows only events belonging to my client organisation
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Requesting another organisation's event directly is refused
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Colleagues in the same client organisation can see the same events

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Can view my current profile details
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Can update name, contact details and communication preferences
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Invalid contact details are rejected with a message explaining why
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Internal users additionally see their department

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Can record event name, purpose, description, proposed date and time, expected attendance, venue requirements, accessibility needs, equipment requirements and whether registration is needed
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Accessibility needs are optional and can be left blank
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: A new request is created as a draft against me and my client organisation, without being submitted for review
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Fields required for submission are identified, but leaving them incomplete does not prevent creating a draft; completeness is checked when submitting

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Can save further changes to an existing draft even when information required for submission is still incomplete
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Can reopen a draft later with all entered information intact and editable
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Drafts are distinguishable from submitted requests in my events list
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Drafts do not appear in the Coordinator's review queue

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given a draft with all mandatory information complete, when I submit it, then it becomes visible to ConnectSphere for review and I can see that it has been submitted
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Given a draft with mandatory information missing, when I submit it, then submission is refused, the outstanding items are listed, and the request remains a draft
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Given a submitted request that has not been returned for clarification, when I try to edit it directly, then editing is refused

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: My events list shows each request with its name, proposed date, current state and assigned coordinator once one exists
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Can filter the list by state
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Selecting an event opens its full details
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Where the event is waiting on me, this is apparent from the list

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Can delete a request that is still a draft, after confirming
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Deleting is not offered once a request has been submitted

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Only Technical Support Staff can assign an Event Coordinator to a submitted request
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: The assigned coordinator becomes responsible for the event and it appears in their list
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: I can see who my coordinator is and how to contact them
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: The assignment is recorded with the user who made it and when

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Only Technical Support Staff can reassign an event to another Event Coordinator
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: The new coordinator gains coordinator rights and the previous one loses them
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: The Event Organiser can see the new contact
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: The previous assignment remains visible in the event history

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Can open a request assigned to me and view all information the Event Organiser submitted
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: When I open a submitted request to review it, its status becomes Under Review and is visible to the Event Organiser
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Cannot review a request assigned to another Event Coordinator

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given a request assigned to me, when I return it for clarification with a message, then the Event Organiser is notified and can see my questions and that a response is needed
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Given a returned request, the Event Organiser can amend and resubmit it, after which it returns to my review queue and I am notified
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: The clarification exchange remains visible against the event record

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given a request I am reviewing, when I approve it, then planning activities become available for that event and the Organiser can see it was approved
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Given a request I am reviewing, when I reject it, then I must give a reason, the reason is visible to the Organiser, and no venue or equipment can be reserved against the event afterwards
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Given any decision, the decision, who made it and when are recorded

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: The event shows a single current state, in language that does not assume knowledge of ConnectSphere's internal process
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Where the event is waiting on someone, the event shows who
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: The state shown is consistent with the actions that have actually been taken on the event

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given an approved event I coordinate, when I change information on it, then the change is saved and the previous value, my identity and the time are recorded
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Given an edit affects existing venue, equipment or registration arrangements, when I save it, then the affected arrangements are identified for rechecking and I am warned before the change takes effect
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: After saving an edit with affected arrangements, those arrangements are marked outstanding and the event is in Planning until they have been rechecked and settled
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: While planning an event I coordinate, I can set or update its registration capacity and opening and closing times when registration is needed
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: Given an event that has been cancelled or completed, when I try to change it, then the change is refused

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: History shows each recorded action with the user and the time, most recent first
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: For a changed value, the history shows what it was and what it became
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Attendees and unrelated Event Organisers cannot see the history

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: As a Coordinator, I see requests awaiting my review and my assigned events
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: As Venue Staff, I see venue booking requests awaiting my decision
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: As Technical Support Staff, I see equipment requests awaiting my decision
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Selecting an item opens the relevant event or request

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Can create and update a venue with location, capacity, facilities, accessibility features and operating information
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Updates are reflected in venue search
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Users who are not Venue Staff cannot create or edit venues

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Can record the supported layouts for a venue
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Supported layouts are shown on the venue's details
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: A venue that does not support a required layout is not offered as matching that requirement

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Availability is shown across a chosen date range, reflecting existing bookings and recorded unavailability
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Each entry shows what is occupying the venue and when
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Attendees and Event Organisers cannot see the internal availability view

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given a venue with no booking in a period, when I block that period with a reason, then the venue is shown as unavailable then and is not returned by venue search
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Given a period already holding a confirmed booking, when I try to block it, then the block is refused and the conflicting booking is identified (superseded by SG2-80, Week 7 change #2: such a period can now be blocked and its bookings are flagged as affected)
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Given a block I have created, when I remove it, then the venue becomes available for that period again

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Opening venue search from an approved event pre-fills the criteria from that event's requirements
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Can filter by date, time, attendance, location, capacity, accessibility, layout and facilities, and only venues meeting all applied criteria and free at that time are returned
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Accessibility is used as a matching requirement only when accessibility needs have been specified for the event
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: When nothing matches, this is stated and the current search criteria are shown

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given expected attendance above the venue's capacity, when I view that venue against the event, then it is flagged unsuitable and the reason is stated
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Given a required facility the venue lacks, when I view that venue against the event, then the missing facility is identified and booking is blocked; no exception is permitted
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: A capacity exception can be approved by Venue Staff, Technical Support Staff or the Event Organiser for the event; the approval and approver are recorded against the booking request. A coordinator acknowledging the warning alone does not approve an exception
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: When no accessibility needs are specified, missing accessibility features do not make the venue unsuitable; when needs are specified, any missing features are identified in the suitability check
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: Approval of a capacity exception does not approve the booking; Venue Staff still decide on the booking request

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Can request a chosen venue for an approved event, carrying the event timing, required layout and venue requirements
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: The request reaches Venue Staff and awaits their decision
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: The request is shown as pending while awaiting a decision; it does not hold the venue or block its availability. The venue is committed to the event only when the request is approved
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: An event can have requests for several different venues (Week 7 change #3); a duplicate request for the same venue and an overlapping period is refused

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given an outstanding request with no booking conflict, all required facilities available and either sufficient capacity or a recorded capacity exception approved by Venue Staff, Technical Support Staff or the Event Organiser for the event, when I approve it, then the venue is committed to that event and the coordinator is notified
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Given an outstanding request, when I reject it, then I must give a reason, the request is marked rejected, and the coordinator can see the reason
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Given any decision, the decision, who made it and when are recorded

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: I can mark a venue unavailable for a period, choosing a reason (maintenance, equipment failure, renovation, safety concern, other) and adding a note
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Marking is allowed even when confirmed bookings fall within the period
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Bookings that fall within the period are identified and flagged as affected by venue unavailability
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Affected events are not cancelled automatically, and their original event information is kept
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: During the period, the venue appears as unavailable and is not returned by venue search
acceptanceCriteria.AC6: The unavailability, its reason, who recorded it and when are all recorded

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Blocking a period that contains confirmed bookings is no longer refused; the bookings are flagged as affected instead (see SG2-80)
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: SG2-45 AC1 (blocked venue is shown as unavailable and excluded from search) and AC3 (removing a block restores availability) still hold
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Existing blocks are kept as venue unavailability records
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Tests for SG2-45 AC2 are replaced with the new behaviour; the rest of the SG2-45 tests still pass

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: I can place a hold on a venue for an event and a period, and I must set an expiry date/time that is in the future
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: A hold cannot be created without an expiry
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: While the hold is active, the venue is shown as held for that period, and other requests for that period are reported as conflicts with the hold
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: A hold is shown as "Tentative", never as a confirmed booking, and does not count as an approved venue booking when the event is confirmed
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: A hold can be turned into a confirmed booking through the normal approval process before it expires, or released early
acceptanceCriteria.AC6: The Event Coordinator is notified when a hold is placed, including its expiry

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given an active hold whose expiry time has passed without being converted to a confirmed booking, the hold's status becomes Expired
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Once a hold has expired, the venue becomes available for other requests for that period
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: An expired hold is never treated as a confirmed booking and cannot be approved; a new request is needed
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: The Event Coordinator is warned before the hold expires (e.g. 24 hours before; confirm the lead time with the customer) and notified again when it expires
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: The expiry is recorded in the event's history

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: I can delete a venue that has no current or future bookings, holds or pending booking requests; otherwise the deletion is refused and what blocks it is listed
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: A deleted venue no longer appears in venue search, availability or new booking requests, while past bookings and event history keep its name
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: I can change an active hold's expiry to another time in the future; a hold that has expired, been converted or been released cannot be changed
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: When a hold's expiry changes, the Event Coordinator is notified of the new expiry, and the warning before expiry (SG2-85) is based on the new time
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: Only Venue Staff can delete venues or change hold expiries, and each action is recorded with who did it and when

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Submission requires: event name, purpose, description, proposed date and time, expected attendance, venue requirements, preferred room layout, accessibility needs, equipment requirements, and whether registration is needed
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Accessibility needs and equipment requirements can be answered "None", but cannot be left blank
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Submitting with any of these missing is refused, every missing item is listed, and the request stays a draft (as SG2-30 AC2)
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Drafts can still be saved with these fields incomplete (SG2-28 AC4 and SG2-29 unchanged)
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: Requests already submitted are not affected

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Can see how many have registered and how many places remain for an event I organise or coordinate
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Can see the list of registered attendees
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: An Event Organiser sees this only for their own organisation's events
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Attendee contact details are shown only to users authorised to see them
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: As the Event Organiser, I can set the registration capacity and the opening and closing times for my event, and change them at any time before the event starts, including after it is confirmed
acceptanceCriteria.AC6: As the Event Organiser, I can close registration early, reopen it or extend it
acceptanceCriteria.AC7: A capacity above the venue's capacity shows a warning but is allowed
acceptanceCriteria.AC8: The assigned Event Coordinator can view the registration settings but not change them (replaces SG2-39 AC4)
acceptanceCriteria.AC9: Each change to the registration settings is recorded with who made it and when
acceptanceCriteria.AC10: When registration opens or closes (on schedule or closed early by the Organiser), the Event Organiser and the assigned Event Coordinator are notified

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given a venue committed to an event for a period, when a request is raised for an overlapping period at that venue, then the conflict is reported and the conflicting booking is identified
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Given a request in conflict, when approval is attempted, then approval is refused while the conflict stands
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Given a booking that is rejected or cancelled, when the period is next checked, then it no longer causes a conflict

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Can cancel a committed booking, giving a reason
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: The venue becomes available for that period again
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: On an event with several venue bookings (Week 7 change #3), releasing one booking leaves the event's other bookings unchanged
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: The coordinator and Event Organiser are notified
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: The cancellation and its reason are recorded

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given a venue record, when I set a setup time and a turnaround time in minutes, then both are saved against that venue and shown on the venue's details
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Setup and turnaround times can be configured separately for each venue
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: A venue with no value set defaults to 0 minutes of setup and turnaround
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Negative values are refused
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: I can record a venue's emergency access arrangements and any known restrictions (e.g. maximum occupancy for a given layout, prohibited equipment, access limits); these are shown on the venue's details and in the Safety Officer's view of the event (SG2-91), or as "Not recorded" if missing
acceptanceCriteria.AC6: Only Venue Staff can change a venue's setup time, turnaround time or safety details, and each change is recorded with who made it and when

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given an event from 10:00 to 12:00 at a venue with 30 minutes of setup and 45 minutes of turnaround, the booking is treated as occupying the venue from 09:30 to 12:45
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Given a booking request whose effective period (including setup and turnaround) overlaps another booking's effective period at the same venue, the conflict is reported and the conflicting booking is identified
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: The venue availability view shows setup and turnaround periods as occupied, marked separately from the event itself
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Venue search does not return a venue whose effective period clashes with the requested time
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: Advertised event start and end times shown to Organisers and Attendees are unchanged

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given existing bookings whose effective periods now overlap, when setup/turnaround times are introduced or changed for a venue, then the affected bookings are flagged as conflicting
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Flagged bookings are not cancelled, removed or altered automatically
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Venue Staff and the assigned Event Coordinator of each affected event can see a list of the flagged bookings and which booking each one clashes with
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: The assigned Event Coordinator of each affected event is notified
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: A flag clears once the conflict is resolved (e.g. a booking is moved, cancelled, or the times are changed)

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Event Coordinator Lead and Safety Officer are available as account roles alongside the existing five roles
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: An account holding either role can reach only the functions for that role; any other action is refused on the server side
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: The role is shown on the user's profile
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Users in the existing roles are unaffected

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: An Event Coordinator can review, update, request venues/equipment for, and confirm only the events currently assigned to them
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Any attempt to act on an event that isn't assigned to them is refused on the server side
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Once an event is reassigned, the previous coordinator can no longer act on it
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Events in the unassigned queue cannot be acted on by any Event Coordinator

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Technical Support Staff can no longer assign or reassign Event Coordinators; any such attempt is refused on the server side
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Assignments already made under SG2-33/34 stay in place, and their history is kept
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: The Event Organiser can still see who their coordinator is and how to contact them (SG2-33, AC3 still holds)
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Tests from SG2-33/34 are updated to the new role and pass

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: public.event_status contains unassigned, awaiting_safety_check, safety_rejected and preparation, with all 14 values present in a fresh CI database
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Submitting a complete draft returns 200 with request.status === 'unassigned'; no row is left in 'submitted' with a null coordinator_id after the backfill
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Assigning a coordinator on an unassigned event moves it to submitted; assigning on an already-advanced event leaves its status unchanged
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: canTransition returns true for exactly the edges in the status flow diagram and false for every other ordered pair, including every pair whose source is completed or cancelled
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: GET the event stage returns the exact stage, stage_key and waiting_on values for unassigned, awaiting_safety_check, safety_rejected and preparation, and a stepper_steps array of length 7; planning returns stage 'Arrangements' with stage_key 'in_planning'
acceptanceCriteria.AC6: Marking an event Completed by the assigned coordinator on a confirmed or preparation event whose end time has passed returns 200 with status 'completed' and completed_by/completed_at populated
acceptanceCriteria.AC7: A completed event is refused by further planning updates, is absent from the work queue, and remains readable via the event and history endpoints
acceptanceCriteria.AC8: Each new lifecycle transition appends exactly one event_audit_logs row with the correct old_value/new_value/actor_id; a failed audit insert does not fail the transition
acceptanceCriteria.AC9: EventDetail and the 7-step stepper render without layout breakage or horizontal overflow at 390x844 and 1440x900
acceptanceCriteria.AC10: npm run ci is green with 100% per-file statement, branch, line and function coverage in both server and client
acceptanceCriteria.AC11: All four DoD category tags appear in the new tests and in the PR Test Case Inventory table; every commit carries [SG2-100]
acceptanceCriteria.AC12: The e2e regression journeys for this story pass and are registered in docs/regression-cases.json
acceptanceCriteria.AC13: No secrets are committed; every new route is permission-gated server-side; every new write repeats its guards as conditions on the update itself

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Can create and update equipment with type, description, quantity held, location and operational status
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Equipment recorded as damaged or under maintenance is excluded from what is treated as available
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Users who are not Technical Support Staff cannot edit equipment records

stories.source: Live Jira SG2-52 description verified in Google Chrome on 7 October 2026.

stories.summary: Record what equipment an event needs

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Can record required equipment against an approved event, with type, quantity and technical notes
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Can amend the requirements while they are still being arranged
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: A quantity that is not a positive number is refused
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: The request reaches Technical Support Staff
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: Technical Support Staff can record updates on the request as equipment is arranged, including any shortfall, and the coordinator can see these updates
acceptanceCriteria.AC6: For each requested item, Technical Support Staff can record where it will be placed (which venue and position within it), for the Safety Officer review (Week 7 change #6, SG2-91); an item with no placement recorded is shown as Not recorded

stories.source: Live Jira SG2-53 description verified in the in-app browser on 8 October 2026. AC numbering follows displayed bullet order.

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: The event shows whether every venue booking it needs is approved (an event may have several, per Week 7 change #3), whether any requested equipment is reserved, and whether registration capacity and opening/closing times are set when registration is needed
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Each required arrangement is labelled ready or outstanding; equipment and registration are labelled not required when they are not needed
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: When all required arrangements are ready, the event is shown as ready for confirmation

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: When an event request is submitted, it enters the unassigned queue instead of going straight to an Event Coordinator
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Only the Event Coordinator Lead can view the queue
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Each queue entry shows basic event information (name, organiser, proposed date/time, expected attendance, submitted date)
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Requests in the queue show as Unassigned to the Event Organiser
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: An event leaves the queue once it has been assigned

stories.summary: Check whether the equipment is there to give

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Checking availability shows the quantity held, the quantity already committed to overlapping events, and what remains
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Equipment recorded as damaged or under maintenance is not counted as available
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Where the request exceeds what remains, the shortfall is stated

stories.source: Live Jira SG2-54 description verified in the in-app browser on 9 October 2026. AC numbering follows displayed bullet order.

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Can reserve equipment for an event where enough remains free
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Reserving reduces what is available to overlapping events
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Reserving more than remains free is refused
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: The reservation is visible on the event, and the coordinator is notified

stories.source: Live SG2-55 Jira description, bullet order, read in the in-app browser.

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Cancelling an event releases the equipment reserved for it
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Releasing a reservation returns equipment to the available quantity for that period only if it is operational and not committed elsewhere; damaged equipment or equipment under maintenance remains unavailable
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: The release is recorded against the event

stories.source: Live SG2-56 Jira description, bullet order, read through the Atlassian connector.

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given an event I coordinate with every required venue booking approved, any requested equipment reserved, and registration capacity and opening/closing times set if registration is needed, when I confirm it, then its status becomes Confirmed and the Event Organiser can see the confirmed arrangements and is notified
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Given an event with any of these required arrangements outstanding (including any one of several venue bookings), when I try to confirm it, confirmation is refused and the outstanding items are listed; equipment or registration that is not required does not block confirmation
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Given a confirmed event for which registration is required, attendees can register once the registration period is open

stories.source: SG2-58 Jira acceptance criteria as recorded in the team's implementation contract; AC numbering follows displayed bullet order. Product-owner decisions: confirm only from Preparation; equipment must be reserved and placed with no shortfall; AC3 is delivered as the open-for-registration rule (SG2-60 builds registration).

stories.summary: Be told when something affects my event

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: A notification is raised for the users affected when an event is submitted, a coordinator is assigned, clarification is requested, a decision is made on a request or booking, an event is confirmed, a significant change is accepted, or an event is cancelled
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Each notification identifies the event, says what happened, and when
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Users with no relationship to the event are not notified

stories.source: SG2-68 Jira acceptance criteria as recorded in the team's implementation contract; AC numbering follows displayed bullet order. Product-owner scope: submitted, coordinator assigned, clarification requested, event request decision and venue booking decision/hold conversion are built here; event confirmed is SG2-58; significant change accepted (SG2-64/65) and event cancelled (SG2-67) have no code path yet and are recorded as dependencies.

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: I can raise more than one venue booking request for the same event, and each one stays linked to that event
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Each venue is checked independently for suitability, availability (including setup/turnaround) and conflicts
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: A problem with one venue does not block requests for the event's other venues
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: The event shows all of its venue bookings and the status of each one
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: The event's venue arrangement counts as ready only when every venue booking the event needs is approved

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Event list, event detail, venue availability, equipment and registration screens are readable and usable on a phone-sized screen without sideways scrolling
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Event Organisers can create, save, reopen, edit and submit their event requests on a phone without sideways scrolling
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Layouts adapt on larger screens rather than stretching
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Controls can be operated by touch

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: From the unassigned queue, I can assign an event to an Event Coordinator
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: I can reassign an assigned event to a different Event Coordinator; the new coordinator gains rights to manage it and the previous coordinator loses them
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Only the Event Coordinator Lead can assign or reassign events
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: The newly assigned coordinator, any previous coordinator, and the Event Organiser are notified of an assignment or reassignment
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: Each assignment and reassignment is recorded with who made it and when, and previous assignments stay visible in the event history

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given a booking for an event I coordinate that is affected by venue unavailability, I am notified with the venue, the period and the reason
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: The event shows that alternative venue arrangements are required, and the venue booking is shown as outstanding
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Original event information (date, time, attendance, requirements) is kept unchanged
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: From the affected event, I can search for alternative venues using the event's existing requirements and raise a booking request for a replacement venue
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: Once the replacement booking is approved, the affected booking is released and the event no longer shows alternative arrangements as required
acceptanceCriteria.AC6: If the affected event is Confirmed or in Preparation, it moves back to Planning (SG2-66), and the Event Organiser is notified that the venue arrangement is being changed

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given a change to information the customer regards as significant, when I open the request, then the affected venue bookings, equipment reservations and registrations are listed as requiring revalidation
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Given a change raising attendance above a booked venue's capacity, that booking is flagged for a new capacity check; any capacity exception for the revised attendance is decided by Venue Staff
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Given a change to the date or time, the venue bookings and equipment reservations are flagged for rechecking against the new period
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Given I accept a change with affected arrangements, those arrangements are marked outstanding and the event returns to Planning until they have been rechecked and settled. This applies to Confirmed events and events in Awaiting Safety Check or Preparation too: any safety approval is withdrawn and the event must pass every check again before it can be confirmed (SG2-94 AC3)
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: Only Venue Staff can approve a capacity exception, for change requests and for new booking requests alike; an attempt by Technical Support Staff, the Event Organiser or any other role is refused on the server side (403), and Venue Staff's booking approval accepts only an exception recorded by Venue Staff. This replaces the wider approver list in SG2-47 AC3 and SG2-49 AC1 (see the decisions recorded on those stories)
acceptanceCriteria.AC6: Once an event is Confirmed or in Preparation, its details cannot be edited directly: a direct planning edit is refused on the server side with a message pointing to a change request (SG2-64). Registration settings are the exception (SG2-63). This replaces the direct-edit rule in SG2-39 for those statuses
acceptanceCriteria.AC7: The Event Organiser and the assigned Event Coordinator are notified when an event goes back to Planning, and the move is recorded in the event history

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: The Event Organiser asks for cancellation, giving a reason, and only the assigned Event Coordinator carries it out, provided the event is not already completed or cancelled; a direct cancellation by the Organiser or any other role is refused on the server side
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Cancelling releases all of the event's venue bookings (SG2-82) and its equipment reservations (SG2-56)
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Registered attendees are notified
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: The reason, who cancelled it and when are recorded
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: A cancelled event cannot be reinstated; a similar event needs a new request

stories.source: Live SG2-67 Jira description, bullet order, read through the Atlassian connector.

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: When all of an event's venue bookings are approved and its required equipment is reserved, the event's status becomes Awaiting Safety Check
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: The Safety Officer can see a list of events awaiting a check
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Each event shows the information needed for the review: expected attendance, venue capacity and layout, emergency access, accessibility requirements, equipment and where it will be placed, expected crowd movement, and known venue restrictions
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Only Safety Officers can open the safety check list

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: For an event awaiting a check, I can record one of three decisions: Approve, Reject, or Request Changes
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Reject and Request Changes require me to give a reason, and Request Changes also requires me to name the arrangements to change (venue, equipment/technical, or other)
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: On Approve, the event can move on to Preparation
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: On Reject, the event is shown as Safety Rejected, cannot move on to Preparation, and goes back to Planning so the coordinator can rework the arrangements and resubmit them for a new check (the status flow allows safety_rejected → planning)
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: The assigned Event Coordinator and the Event Organiser are notified of the decision and its reason
acceptanceCriteria.AC6: Each decision is recorded with who made it, when, and the reason

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given an event with no approved safety check, any attempt to move it to Preparation is refused on the server side, and the reason is shown
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Given an event whose most recent safety decision is Approve, it can move to Preparation
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: If a significant change (date/time, attendance, venue, equipment) is accepted after safety approval, the approval is withdrawn and the event must be checked again
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: The event's status and its outstanding items show the safety check as a step
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: Given an event whose most recent safety decision is not Approve, when the Event Coordinator tries to confirm it, then confirmation is refused on the server side and the safety check is listed among the outstanding items; the coordinator can confirm only once the Safety Officer has approved. This supersedes SG2-58 AC1, which allowed confirmation on venue and equipment alone
acceptanceCriteria.AC6: Registration settings do not block confirmation: an event that needs registration can be confirmed before its capacity and times are set, and Attendees can register only once the Event Organiser has set them and registration is open (SG2-63). This supersedes the registration condition in SG2-57 AC1 and SG2-58 AC1/AC2

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Unread notifications are countable at a glance from anywhere in the system
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: The notification list shows newest first, and distinguishes read from unread
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Opening a notification takes me to the event it concerns and marks it read
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Can clear the unread state for everything at once
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: As an Event Coordinator, I receive reminders for each upcoming event I coordinate that still has outstanding arrangements (SG2-57), listing what is outstanding
acceptanceCriteria.AC6: I can set how often these reminders come (daily by default); they stop once every arrangement is ready, or the event is cancelled or completed
acceptanceCriteria.AC7: Users unrelated to the event receive no reminders

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: An account can hold more than one of the seven roles, and can reach the functions of every role it holds
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Every server-side check still applies per action and per event; for example, an Event Coordinator who is also an Event Organiser can still act as coordinator only on events assigned to them
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: The user's profile shows every role the account holds
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: Existing single-role accounts keep working unchanged
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: Tests cover an account holding two roles, for both permitted and refused actions
acceptanceCriteria.AC6: Reading an event's stage or change history requires a relationship to that event (its Organiser, its assigned Event Coordinator, a Lead, or a role that works on its venues, equipment or safety check); an Event Coordinator not assigned to the event is refused by ID, and a reassigned coordinator loses access immediately. Tests cover assigned, unrelated and reassigned coordinators

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Can search by event name and client organisation
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: Can filter by date, state, venue, category and assigned coordinator
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: Results include only events I am permitted to see
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: When nothing matches, this is stated along with the filters in force

acceptanceCriteria.AC1: Given an event with several venue bookings, when I change or cancel one of them, the event's other venue bookings stay unchanged
acceptanceCriteria.AC2: The other bookings are removed only if I explicitly choose to cancel them too
acceptanceCriteria.AC3: The cancelled venue becomes available again for that period (including its setup/turnaround time)
acceptanceCriteria.AC4: The change or cancellation, its reason, who made it and when are all recorded, and Venue Staff for the affected venue are notified
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: Only the assigned Event Coordinator can cancel or release a venue booking; an attempt by Venue Staff or any other role is refused on the server side and in the database. This replaces Venue Staff release in SG2-51; Venue Staff record operational problems by marking the venue unavailable (SG2-80) instead
acceptanceCriteria.AC6: SG2-51 tests that expect Venue Staff to release a booking are updated to expect refusal
acceptanceCriteria.AC7: If the event is Confirmed or in Preparation, cancelling or changing one venue sends that venue back through change approval and returns the event to Planning (SG2-66), while the event's other venue bookings stay intact
